- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling sharply.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next period; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is neutral or mixed, consider mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates near end of period (last 5–7 days) — increase forecast slightly in final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model may lag — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to capture sentiment shift.
- Avoid forecasting below 50% of recent 18-day low if sentiment is positive — may indicate overcorrection or panic sell-off.
